Brand color compliance validation rules
nodes.rationale: Ratios (60-70% primary, 20-30% secondary, 5-10% accent, max 20% off-brand tolerance) are enforced so brand recognizability stays high while still allowing supporting-palette variety across designs.

nodes.label: Mission→Vision→Value Prop→Positioning→Key Messages→Proof Points chain
nodes.rationale: Ordering messaging as a top-down pipeline (mission to proof points) ensures every downstream message can be traced back to a reason-to-believe, keeping marketing copy differentiated and credible rather than generic.

nodes.label: Message architecture (primary + supporting messages by audience)
Type scale (Major Third ratio, Inter font)
Voice vs. Tone distinction
nodes.rationale: Voice (personality) is kept constant while tone (its expression) is allowed to shift per context, e.g. celebratory in a win announcement vs empathetic in a support reply, so the brand stays recognizable yet situationally appropriate.

nodes.label: Voice development process (traits → chart → context adaptation)
Automation types overview (Hooks/Subagents/Skills/Plugins/MCP)
nodes.rationale: Categorizing automations by mechanism (event-triggered hooks, parallel specialized subagents, packaged-workflow skills, bundled plugins, external-integration MCP servers) lets a codebase signal map cleanly onto the automation type that actually addresses it, avoiding generic one-size-fits-all recommendations.

nodes.label: Recommender workflow (analyze codebase → generate recs → report)
Decision framework: when to recommend each automation type
Model selection guide (haiku/sonnet/opus trade-offs)
nodes.rationale: Model choice trades thoroughness against cost/speed: haiku for fast cheap repetitive checks, sonnet as the balanced recommended default for most review/analysis, opus reserved for complex migrations or architectural reasoning where depth matters more than latency.

design-system skill (token architecture + component specs + slides)
Three-layer token architecture (Primitive→Semantic→Component)
nodes.rationale: Layering tokens as primitive (raw values) → semantic (purpose aliases) → component (component-specific) decouples raw values from meaning and usage, enabling instant theme switching (e.g. dark mode via semantic overrides) and a design-to-code handoff where nothing is hardcoded.

watch debounce mechanism
nodes.rationale: Debounce (default 3s) waits until file activity stops before triggering, so a wave of parallel agent writes doesn't trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Discrete confidence-score rubric
nodes.rationale: Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; the bimodal distribution observed in production (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) shows range guidance collapses to a binary, hence fixed rubric values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) instead of a free 0-1 scale.

nodes.label: Node ID format ({stem}_{entity})
nodes.rationale: Must match the ID the AST extractor generates (full repo-relative path, every directory level kept) so semantic and AST extraction agree on the same node instead of creating orphan ghost-duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: Monorepo multi-subfolder extraction pattern
nodes.rationale: Running the skill pipeline separately on each subfolder would clobber the same graphify-out/ output dir, so the CLI is invoked directly per subfolder (writing graphify-out inside each scanned path) and the resulting graphs are merged afterward at the project root.

nodes.label: Constrained query vocabulary expansion (Step 0)
nodes.rationale: graphify's query CLI matches via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming/synonyms/cross-language match, so a literal user query in different vocabulary than the graph's labels returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise; expanding against the actual graph vocabulary first (never inventing tokens) fixes this.

nodes.label: graphify reflect / LESSONS.md work memory
nodes.rationale: save-result with --outcome useful|dead_end|corrected closes a self-improving feedback loop: reflect reads it back into preferred sources, known dead ends, and prior corrections for the next session.

nodes.label: graphify.build.build_merge
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction (calls/implements/imports) is preserved, and replace-on-re-extract drops every source_file present in new_chunks from the base before merging so stale nodes don't survive a changed file.

nodes.label: graphify.cli._stamped_manifest_files
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files (docs/papers/images) that actually produced output this run get stamped; a changed doc whose chunk failed stays unstamped so the next --update re-queues it instead of silently losing its content.

nodes.label: Track A - Reka UI overlays (data-state + tw-animate-css)
nodes.rationale: Reka's Presence (usePresence) watches for a real CSS animationend/animationcancel event before removing a closing element from the DOM; giving the closing state a data-[state=closed]:animate-out class makes Reka automatically delay unmount until the animation finishes. This only works with `animation`, not `transition` - a plain transition-* class never fires animationend.

nodes.label: Motion timing table (durations/easings)
nodes.rationale: An established rhythm (duration-200 overlays, 700ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) scroll reveals) should be reused rather than picking arbitrary numbers per component - inconsistent motion reads as sloppier than no motion at all.

nodes.label: Tooltip Track A recipe
nodes.rationale: Reka's Tooltip uses data-[state=delayed-open], not data-[state=open] - the data-state value varies by primitive and must be checked in devtools.

nodes.label: Route/page transitions (NuxtPage)
nodes.rationale: Nuxt's <NuxtPage> transition drives Vue's native <Transition>, which is CSS-class-based - Track A territory even though it isn't a Reka component, because Nuxt owns mount/unmount timing the same way Reka does.

nodes.label: The ladder (YAGNI-first decision rungs)
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: does this need to exist at all, is it already in the codebase, does stdlib do it, does a native platform feature cover it, does an already-installed dependency solve it, can it be one line - only then write the minimum code that works.

nodes.label: `ponytail:` shortcut comment convention
nodes.rationale: Marks deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (e.g. global lock, O(n^2) scan) and names the upgrade trigger, so the shortcut is tracked instead of silently rotting.

nodes.label: ponytail-gain skill (measured-impact scoreboard)
nodes.rationale: Figures are published benchmark medians across 5 tasks and 3 models, not computed from the current repo - the skill deliberately never prints a per-repo savings number since the unbuilt version was never written.

nodes.label: Layout selection by use case (25 layouts)
Duarte Sparkline pattern
nodes.rationale: Alternates 'What Is' (current pain) and 'What Could Be' (better future) with pattern breaks at the 1/3 and 2/3 positions to create engagement peaks, resolving into 'New Bliss'.
